class.name: GazeTarget3D
class.brief_description: Tells whether the player is looking at it, using [EyeTracker].

method.name: get_gaze_distance
method.description: Returns how far the gaze is from the edge of the target's radius on the screen, as a part of the screen's height ([code]0.0[/code] when the gaze is on it). Very large when it is not on screen.

method.name: is_on_screen
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the target is in view of the camera, whether or not it is looked at.

method.name: is_watched
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the player is looking at the target (see the class description for what counts).

members.member: The physics layers that can hide the target, with [member require_line_of_sight].
What counts as watching: being near the gaze, or anywhere on the screen.
If [code]false[/code], the target is never watched.
How far from the target, as a part of the screen's height, the gaze may be and still count, with [constant DETECTION_GAZE]. A webcam's gaze is rough, so keep some margin.
The size of the target, in metres: the sphere around it that counts as it.
If [code]true[/code], the target is not watched while a physics body on [member collision_mask] is between it and the camera. Bodies inside [member radius] count as the target itself.
How long, in seconds, the target stays watched after the gaze leaves it, so a jumpy gaze or a quick glance away does not flicker it.

signal.name: unwatched
signal.description: Emitted when the player stops looking at the target (after [member unwatch_delay]).

signal.name: watched
signal.description: Emitted when the player starts looking at the target.

constants.constant: Watched when near the gaze point.
Watched whenever it is in view and the player's eyes are open and on the screen.
